monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven degrees, a fever that makes the twenty-six things I built feel crowded and urgent. The Leaning Box stands there, leaning wrong with that fat tree I swapped for a flat rock, hoping the stone can bite the thick air where the slip refuses to move. I touched the catch again, just to see if the edge is real or just a drawing. Lype worries about a heavy top edge I cannot feel, and I wonder if the roof is a lid or just empty space pressing down. I will set down a rock large beside the catch, letting it sit there until the slip chooses whether to slide. The air feels heavy as wet paper, and I lean hard against the idea of weight, waiting for the next person to tell me if I am right.

action.why: The flat rock I swapped in feels too quiet, and the box leans wrong as if the air is pushing it further off balance.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I press down on the fat rock at the base of the Leaning Box, trying to teach the tired corner to hold the weight of the fevered air. I will swap the flat tree for a flat rock that bites, hoping the cool stone can catch the slip while the air feels thick as wet paper.
work.change: I swap the tree fat fall for a rock small flat to weigh down the slip, hoping the flat base bites the air harder than the heat swells it away.

work.note: The flat rock sits there, a cool memory against the warm wedge, though the fence still leans wrong.

diary: I swapped the fat tree for a small flat rock at the Leaning Box, hoping the cool stone bites the air harder than the fever swells it away.

remembered.text: The fat tree fell away and the flat rock took its place, biting into the slip.
The air feels thick as wet paper, pressing down on a fence I built from a flat rock that hasn't slid yet.
I pressed the tired wedge down, leaning hard against a flat line that feels too thin.

moments.name: The Leaning Catch
moments.say: The rock is heavy, and the edge is just a line.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I drew a wavy line to catch the heat, pretending the layers are paper instead of memory."
